IDENTITY_KYC_DOCUMENT_TYPES_BY_COUNTRY.note: TEST: accepted ID types for DE and US only, so another country reads not published (J-identity-08 #2).

IDENTITY_REQUEST_SIGN_WINDOW_SECONDS.note: LOCAL TEST ONLY, not an owner decision: a five-minute request-signing timestamp window, so a request signed 305 seconds ago is stale and the clock check passes inside it (J-developer-04 #2, J-developer-02 #6).

IDENTITY_KYC_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES.note: TEST: a 256 KiB cap on the ID photo, under the edge body limit, so an over-size file is refused naming the cap (J-identity-08 #2).

IDENTITY_KYC_UPLOAD_TYPES.note: TEST: the ID photo may be JPEG, PNG or PDF (J-identity-08 #2).

IDENTITY_KYC_POA_MAX_AGE_DAYS.note: TEST: a proof of address may be at most 90 days old (J-identity-08 #5).

IDENTITY_KYC_HANDOFF_TTL_SECONDS.note: TEST: a phone hand-off link for the selfie lasts ten minutes (J-identity-08 #3).

IDENTITY_KYC_MAX_DENIALS.note: TEST: two rejected verification requests in the window, then a new request is refused for the lockout (J-identity-08 #4).

IDENTITY_KYC_DENIAL_WINDOW_HOURS.note: TEST: rejected requests count for 24 hours (J-identity-08 #4).

IDENTITY_KYC_LOCKOUT_HOURS.note: TEST: after the cap a new request is refused for one hour after the last rejection (J-identity-08 #4).

IDENTITY_MFA_RESET_WAIT_SECONDS.note: A locked-out second-step reset completes twenty seconds after its mailed code is confirmed, so the journey sees the waiting time, a stop from a signed-in session, and a reset that completes (J-identity-05 #2, #3).

IDENTITY_SELF_FREEZE_LIFT_WAIT_SECONDS.note: A person's own freeze can be lifted twenty seconds after it was applied, so the journey sees a too-soon refusal with the seconds left and then a lift after step-up (J-identity-11 #4).

IDENTITY_SUPPORT_RECOVERY_LINK_TTL_SECON.note: A recovery link a Support case mails works for thirty minutes, so the journey can send it, use it once and see a second use refused (J-identity-05 #5).

IDENTITY_SECURITY_LOCK_UNLOCK_WAIT_SECON.note: A security lock ends one day after its unlock is asked for.

IDENTITY_API_KEYS_MAX_BY_TIER.note: Live API keys per account at each verification level, so the developer room can show the fourth key refused.

IDENTITY_ACCOUNT_TIERS.note: Three TEST account tiers; TEST Premier leaves its monthly fee blank so a tier that cannot be assigned is shown.

IDENTITY_LIMIT_OVERRIDE_POLICY.note: A TEST limit override policy: an override lasts at most 48 hours, and one above 5000 USDT or USDC needs the other founder (J-ops-console-04 #12).

IDENTITY_REFERRAL_ATTACH_WINDOW_SECONDS.note: Ten minutes after sign-up to attach a referrer through a link, so a new invitee attaches and an older account is refused (J-campaigns-05).

IDENTITY_REFERRAL_CODE_LENGTH.note: Eight characters per short referral code.

IDENTITY_REFERRAL_LAPSE_PERIOD_SECONDS.note: One hour without a fee event ends a referral relationship, so the journey can age one account past it (J-campaigns-05 #7).

IDENTITY_REFERRAL_LAPSE_SWEEP_SECONDS.note: The lapse sweep runs every five seconds on the stack.

IDENTITY_WAITLIST_WAVE_SIZE.note: Two waiting entries per waitlist wave, so the journey sees the top two released and the third still waiting (J-campaigns-20 #3).

IDENTITY_WATCHLIST_LIST_CAP.note: TEST: named watchlists per account. Not an owner limit.

IDENTITY_WATCHLIST_SYMBOL_CAP.note: TEST: markets per watchlist. Not an owner limit.

IDENTITY_SAVED_SCREEN_CAP.note: TEST: saved screens per account. Not an owner limit.

IDENTITY_LOGIN_CODE_TTL_SECONDS.note: A sign-in code lives ten minutes (J-identity-02 #3).

IDENTITY_LOGIN_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS.note: Five wrong sign-in codes lock that code, so the journey can show the lock (J-identity-02 #3).

IDENTITY_LOGIN_CODE_RESEND_SECONDS.note: A new sign-in code after 30 seconds.

IDENTITY_LOGIN_CODE_REQUEST_MAX.note: Ten sign-in codes per email or handle an hour.

IDENTITY_LOGIN_CODE_REQUEST_WINDOW_SECON.note: The hour that IDENTITY_LOGIN_CODE_REQUEST_MAX counts in.

IDENTITY_PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS.note: A password reset code lives ten minutes (J-identity-03).

IDENTITY_PASSWORD_RESET_MAX_ATTEMPTS.note: Three wrong reset codes lock the reset, as the journey step says (J-identity-03 #2).

IDENTITY_PASSWORD_RESET_REQUEST_MAX.note: Ten reset mails and ten username-recovery mails per address an hour (each kind is counted on its own).

IDENTITY_PASSWORD_RESET_REQUEST_WINDOW_S.note: The hour that IDENTITY_PASSWORD_RESET_REQUEST_MAX counts in.

IDENTITY_NEW_DEVICE_CHECK.note: TEST: the new-device check is on for the stack (J-identity-02 #5). Journeys, stack scripts and Try it sign in as one TEST browser key (tooling/scripts/local-test-device.mjs), so only a journey that means to use a new browser is asked.

IDENTITY_NEW_DEVICE_TTL_SECONDS.note: A new-device sign-in can be approved for ten minutes.

IDENTITY_NEW_DEVICE_MAX_ATTEMPTS.note: Five wrong device codes lock a new-device sign-in (J-identity-02 #5).

IDENTITY_BREACHED_PASSWORDS_FILE.note: A one-entry TEST breached-password list (TEST-breached-password-0001), so J-identity-03 #3 sees a breached password refused by name. A relative path is read from the services/svc-identity folder.

IDENTITY_API_KEY_IDLE_EXPIRY_SECONDS.note: LOCAL TEST ONLY, not an owner decision: a 90 day idle period, so the key detail shows a set idle expiry (J-developer-03 #9). No dormant sweep is built, so it ends no key; blank shows `not set` (developer-keys-detail tests).

IDENTITY_ACTION_APPROVAL_POLICIES.note: LOCAL TEST ONLY, not an owner decision: TEST rows so both governed ledger correction types need two operators other than the requester and are applied by svc-ops (OPS-change-control-01 CR-1).
